_comment: Committed performance baselines, KEYED BY MACHINE+TOOLCHAIN FINGERPRINT.
A baseline captured on one CPU/compiler says nothing about another: a 2017 Kaby Lake
(AVX2, 4 doubles/reg) and an Apple M4 or an AVX-512 Xeon (8 doubles/reg) are not
comparable. tools/fingerprint.sh computes the key; the perf gate REFUSES to compare
across keys and instead tells you to re-baseline. See CLAUDE.md sections 3 and 4.
'thresholds' are policy and machine-independent: the factor by which we must beat
QuantLib. 'machines.<key>.metrics' hold the measured timings for that fingerprint,
where QuantLib was compiled with the SAME compiler and flags as our engine.
curve_build is measured against QuantLib's GlobalBootstrap -- its OWN global-LM
algorithm on the SAME square problem (same knots, same instruments). It is NOT compared
against IterativeBootstrap: that is a different, cheaper sequential 1-D algorithm which
cannot do the over-determined global fit or supply analytic risk. IterativeBootstrap is
in fact faster on the simple square case; our win is over GlobalBootstrap and, far more,
on the AAD risk ladder (bump-and-reprice-free) and vectorized analytics.
_thresholds_note: min_speedup_vs_quantlib is the HARD, load-ROBUST gate (both sides timed back to back). max_self_regression is advisory: exceeding it only WARNS (absolute ns is load-sensitive on a noisy box); only a GROSS regression (>2x, a real code problem) hard-fails. Tighten/rely on it after a quiesced --update.

metric_descriptions.curve_build: Global-LM calibration of a square curve (23 instruments, 23 knots): ours (AAD Jacobian + templated kernel) vs QuantLib GlobalBootstrap (numerical Jacobian + object pricing)
metric_descriptions.risk_full_jacobian: Full bucketed delta ladder (our AAD + implicit-function-theorem vs QuantLib bump-and-reprice)
metric_descriptions.portfolio_analytics: Par rate + NPV + PV01 across a large swap portfolio (batched vs per-swap loop)
metric_descriptions.warm_recalibration: Stage 2: re-calibrate after a small (in-envelope) market tick -- ours (cached-Jacobian, auto envelope detection) vs QuantLib IterativeBootstrap re-bootstrap

52e94be82bc4.notes: Captured by tools/check_perf.py --update (3 reps, benchmark_min_time=0.5s), machine load ~3. The speedup RATIOS are load-robust (both sides timed together); the absolute ns are not authoritative until re-captured on a quiesced machine.

a8c9a844826e.notes: AVX2 re-baseline (2026-07-29). The `isa` field below reflects the CPU capability (AVX-512), but the engine now BUILDS with AVX2 (256-bit / 4-wide Eigen packets) by default: SWAPS_ENABLE_AVX512 is OFF (cmake/DetectISA.cmake), because heavy AVX-512 DOWNCLOCKS this Intel core and measured SLOWER for the engine's small matrices -- curve_build 813->584us (-28%), risk_full_jacobian 826->497us (-40%), portfolio/warm ~flat. -march=native tuning minus the 512-bit width. Captured by check_perf.py --update (3 reps) with some background load (a concurrent compile); the speedup RATIOS are load-robust, absolute ns best-effort. Turn SWAPS_ENABLE_AVX512=ON to re-test on a core where AVX-512 does not throttle (e.g. AMD Zen4).
